cover: A year on, thousands may still be held
Strike on Mawasi camp kills girl, 7
Plan to curb protests after clashes

stories.label: World · Life & safety · Due process
stories.head: El Fasher, a year after the RSF took it
bullets: Human Rights Watch says thousands of civilians may still be held in RSF detention.
The UN rights office estimates more than 6,000 people were killed in three days of the final offensive.
Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain; the RSF did not respond to its findings.

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Strike on displacement camp kills girl, 7
bullets: Four people, including 7-year-old Jouri al-Soufi, were killed in a strike on a camp in al-Mawasi, Nasser Hospital said.
Israel's military told AFP it was looking into the reports.
Medical sources count 1,559 killed since the ceasefire.

stories.label: India · Due process · Assembly
stories.head: Arrests after Siang dam unrest
bullets: Police say 26 people are arrested over the 23 October arson in Pasighat; eight cases are filed.
Police urged calm and asked people not to share unverified information.
Anti-dam activists Ebo Mili and Otul Jerang reportedly began a hunger strike in custody.

stories.label: World · Assembly · Expression
stories.head: Albania plans curbs on protests
bullets: Police used tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets in weekend clashes in Tirana.
PM Edi Rama's bill would let police limit protests near public institutions and criminalise online calls for violence.
He blamed the opposition and 'foreign actors'; activists warn it threatens assembly and speech.
